AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  JUNE 10, 2026

  SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:00 PM

  Kim Apodaca, Chair
  Rosa Barragan, Vice Chair
  Linda Lopez, Planning Commissioner
  Chris Macias, Planning Commissioner
  Lisa Vernola-Salas, Planning Commissioner

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a
vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.
 CALL TO ORDER

FLAG SALUTE

Commissioner Macias

ROLL CALL OF MEMBERS

Staff Recommendation: That the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. 26-06 to grant a

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  APRIL 22, 2026

The meeting was called to order by Chair Apodaca at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Lopez, Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, and Chair
Apodaca. Vice Chair Barragan was absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Deputy
City Manager; Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager; Anita Lakhani, Deputy City
Attorney, (participated remotely); Gabriel R. Salazar, Senior Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann,
Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of February 25, 2026.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN (PDP) NO. 2026-02
TENTATIVE TRACT MAP (TTM) NO. 2026-03 (85156)
PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 26-02 (SENATE BILL 330)
Matt Hamilton, ADC Norwalk 3, LLC (“Applicant”); a request to demolish an existing
church and school to construct 61 three-story condominium townhomes and associated
site improvements. The subject property at 2.52 acres in size, is located at 12722 Woods
Avenue (also known as Assessor Parcel Numbers (“APN”) 8048-012-014 and 8048-011-
035), located within the Triangle District of the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan (“Specific
Plan”) area.
Environmental: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the project
will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section 15332 (In-Fill
Development Projects) of the CEQA Guidelines. Section 15332 involves in-fill
development within urbanized areas.
The project includes a request for:
(1) PDP No. 2026-02 – to permit the construction of three-story townhome units and
  associated site improvements within a Specific Plan area;
(2) TTM No. 2026-03 (85156) – to consolidate the existing lots and subdivide for
  condominium purposes; and
(3) Planning Application No. 26-02 for a housing development submitted under Senate
  Bill 330.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriel Salazar, Senior Planner,
presented a detailed report on the project. He provided background information stating
that the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan Area No. 18 was adopted by the City Council on
December 2, 2025; that this will be the first project evaluated under this Specific Plan and
is consistent with the General Plan designation of Specific Plan Area No. 18, Triangle
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 22, 2026

District; that the proposed project with sixty-one (61) three-story townhome units is
considered multi-family residential and allowed by right; that the project complies with
applicable City codes, provides adequate parking, vehicular circulation, and pedestrian
access; that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant
to Section 15332 (In-fill Development Projects); that a memorandum was prepared by the
applicant’s consultant demonstrating that the proposed project would not have a
significant effect on the environment; that the project will have a positive impact on the
surrounding neighborhood, revitalize an existing site currently developed with a church
and school facilities, redevelop a public institutional use into housing, diversify housing
stock and improve the economic vitality of the site, in addition to helping the City meet its
Housing Element Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) obligations.

Further, Senior Planner Salazar stated that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning
Commission: (1) Adopt Resolution No. 26-03 to approve Precise Development Plan
(PDP) No. 2026-02 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; (2)
Adopt Resolution No. 26-04 to approve Tentative Tract Map (TTM) No. 2026-03 (85156)
subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (3) Consider and find
that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines pursuant to Section 15332 (In-Fill Development Projects).

Matt Hamilton stated that he is the project applicant and property owner; that, first, he
would like to thank staff for all their efforts in getting them to this point; that, as stated, this
is the first project implemented under the newly adopted Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan;
that the project will revitalize the subject property but will also be the catalyst for additional
redevelopment in the area; that they contacted all of the surrounding properties advising
them of their plans and asking them if they were interested in selling their properties to
allow them to extend their project; that the feedback was overwhelmingly positive; that
the project will be environmentally friendly; that the amenities include solar on all the
homes, electrical vehicle charging, efficient appliances, low-flow fixtures, drought-tolerant
landscaping, lots of different green features, besides being exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act. Further, he indicated that their CEQA consultant from EPD
Solutions is in attendance should the Commission have any CEQA-related questions; and
that they are very excited to move forward with the project and start construction.

Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager, stated that staff revised the resolutions; that
they added some findings and language to clarify that the project was cleared by the Fire
Department and added conditions related to that, and that staff provided the applicant
with a copy of the revised conditions.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Apodaca closed
the public hearing.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 22, 2026

Chair Apodaca stated that the project is a quality project which is going to be a nice
addition to the area.

It was moved by Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Macias to: (1) Adopt
Resolution No. 26-03 to approve Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2026-02 subject
to the revised Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; (2) Adopt Resolution No.
26-04 to approve Tentative Tract Map (TTM) No. 2026-03 (85156) subject to the revised
Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (3) Consider and find that the project
is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to
Section 15332 (In-Fill Development Projects).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Lopez, Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-
  Salas, and Chair Apodaca
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Vice Chair Barragan

INFORMATIONAL REPORT – 11606 FIRESTONE BLVD. (ABBEY ROAD PROJECT)

Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager, stated that this informational report is
regarding a property located at 11606 Firestone Boulevard; that the project was submitted
under Assembly Bill 2011; that this Bill was established by the State and introduced as a
streamlined ministerially approval process for multi-family housing for development
projects on commercially-zoned land with one hundred percent (100%) affordable units;
that according to the Norwalk Municipal Code, a Conditional Use Permit and Precise
Development Plan are required; that the application has been streamlined to a ministerial
review under Assembly Bill 2011; that the developer, Abbey Road, Inc. proposes to
construct a four-story, 90-unit affordable apartment complex; that Planning staff did issue
a Notice of Action to ministerially approve this project on April 16, 2026; and that it is
staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission receive and file the presentations
from staff and the applicant.

Maura Johnson, Director of Housing for Abbey Road, a regional non-profit developer of
affordable housing, stated that she is very excited to be working with the City of Norwalk
on the proposed development at 11606 Firestone Boulevard; that, for background
information, Abbey Road and their service provider, partner and parent company, Penny
Lane Centers, began over fifty-five years ago as a foster care provider and continued into
a large behavioral health organization providing services for Los Angeles County hubs
located in North Hollywood, North Hills, Lancaster and Commerce; and that Abbey Road,
a non-profit corporation, was formed in 2009 in response to the need for affordable
housing; that the project will serve homeless transitional aged youth and low-income
families, and will provide on-site supportive services to its residents.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 22, 2026

Dana Sayles, three6ixty, stated that this is their third or fourth project in Norwalk, including
The Walk; that they, too, are excited regarding Abbey Road’s affordable housing project;
that, as staff indicated, the project was processed under the prior General Commercial
(C-3) zoning; and that the application was filed on November 2024, prior to the Specific
Plan being adopted. Further, she went into detail describing the project and stating that
they worked with staff to ensure that the development is designed to be fully consistent
with the Specific Plan.

The project architect, Carlos Garcia, commented on the design of the project stating that
the building massing is modern with angled volumes creating visual interest and dynamic
shadowy patterns setting new high standards for this corridor; that the ground floor is
going to remain active; that the landscaping is extensive; and that they will ensure that
the open spaces are going to be maintained constantly.

All of the Commissioners voiced their support of the project, indicating that it is going to
be a beautiful development, a great addition to the City, and that they are excited to see
the project being developed.

It was moved by Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Macias to receive and
file the presentation presented by staff and the applicants.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Lopez, Commissioner Macias, Commissioner Vernola-
  Salas, and Chair Apodaca
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Vice Chair Barragan

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Planning Commission.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:53 p.m.

SUBJECT:  Time Extension No. 2026-02 - A request to extend entitlements for Conditional Use
  Permit No. 2023-01 and Precise Development Plan No. 2022-03 for one final year
  to allow for a logistics facility operation within a new 76,602 sq. ft. industrial building,
  including associated site improvements at 14516 Carmenita Road (APNs: 8069-
  001-032, 8069-001-033, 8069-001-034, and 8069-001-035)

Request:

That the Planning Commission:

Adopt Resolution No. 26-05 to grant a time extension until July 24, 2027, for Conditional Use Permit
(CUP) No. 2023-01 and Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2022-03 contained in attached
respective Attachment “A”.
Authority:

On July 12, 2023, the Planning Commission adopted resolutions approving CUP No. 2023-01
(Resolution No. 23-16), PDP No. 2022-03 (Resolution No. 23-17), and Lot Merger No. 2022-01
(Resolution No. 23-18). As part of the original approval, a standard condition of approval allowed
for two, one-year extensions to be approved administratively (by the Community Development
Director) and a third and final one-year extension at the discretion of the Planning Commission. This
request excludes an extension for Lot Merger No. 2022-01 as an extension is not required. Lot
mergers are typically administrative approvals that do not expire, but must be recorded.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  June 10, 2026
  Page No. 2

Background:

The subject property is located at 14516 Carmenita Road, on the east side of Carmenita Road, and
north of Pumice Street. Currently, the site contains five buildings totaling 44,557 sq. ft. and remains
idle with fencing around the site. It has a zoning designation of Heavy Manufacturing (M-2) and a
General Plan designation of Heavy Industrial. The subject site is 3.34 acres and is legally described
by Assessor Parcel Numbers (APN) 8069-001-032, 8069-001-033, 8069-001-034, and 8069-001-
035.

CUP No. 2023-01 was approved by the Planning Commission to allow for a logistics facility in the
M-2 Zone and PDP No. 2022-01 approved the construction of a 76,602 sq. ft. industrial building,
including associated site improvements. The project included 77 parking spaces.

The following table provides a chronological history of the actions taken in relation to the subject
property:

 Action  Date
 Approval by Planning Commission for CUP No. 2023-01, PDP No. 2022-03  July 12, 2023
 and LM No. 2022-01 to allow a logistics facility within a new 76,602 sq. ft.
 industrial building, including associated site improvements.
 CUP No. 2023-01, PDP No. 2022-03 and LM No. 2022-01 effective date (10  July 24, 2023
 calendar days after appeal period).
 Approval of a one-year administrative extension request.  July 24, 2024
 Approval of a second one-year administrative extension request.  July 24, 2025

Analysis:

The applicant submitted a request to obtain a third and final one-year extension on May 4, 2026
(see Attachment “B”). Their letter indicates that market conditions for the proposed project have
declined in Los Angeles County as the availability rate for such buildings has increased while leasing
rates have decreased. If approved by the Planning Commission, CUP No. 2023-01 and PDP No.
2022-03 would expire on July 24, 2027. This time extension request is the final allowable request.
Environmental Assessment:

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15332, this project
was determined not to have a significant effect on the environment and was listed as a Class 32
Categorical Exemption, which involves in-fill development with urbanized areas.
Recommendation:

Should the Planning Commission approve the applicant’s third and final request to extend the
entitlements for an additional year, the entitlements to commence construction will remain valid until
July 24, 2027.

Dear Director Alex Hamilton & City of Norwalk team,

 On behalf of IDI Logistics, I am writing formally to request a one-year extension to CUP No. 2023-01, PDP No.
2022-03, LM No. 2022-01 as they relate to IDI’s property located at 14516 Carmenita Road in Norwalk.

SUBJECT:  Time Extension No. 2026-03 - A request to extend entitlements for Precise

  additional months to allow for the construction of a new two-story, 8,715 square foot

  required number of parking spaces on property located at 12217 Rosecrans Avenue

Request:

That the Planning Commission:
Adopt Resolution No. 26-06 to grant a time extension until December 14, 2026, for Precise
Development Plan (PDP No. 2022-04 and Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2022-05 contained
in the attached respective Attachment “A”.
Authority:

On June 12, 2023, the Planning Commission approved Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2022-
04, Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2022-05, Tentative Parcel Map (TPM) No. 2022-03, and
Zone Change (ZC) No. 2022-02. Subsequently, on July 18, 2023, the City Council adopted
Ordinance No. 23-1741 to approve ZC No. 2022-02. As part of the original approval, a standard
condition was included allowing for two, one-year extensions to be approved administratively by the
Community Development Director, and a third and final one-year extension at the discretion of the
Planning Commission. This request excludes an extension for ZC No. 2022-02 as there is no
 Norwalk Planning Commission  June 10, 2026

expiration date. This request also excludes an extension for TPM No. 2022-03 as the Tentative
Parcel Map was recorded within two years of the Planning Commission approval date.
Background:

The subject property is a 0.52-acre project site located at 12217 Rosecrans Avenue. The project
site is located at the northeast corner of Rosecrans Avenue and Norwalk Boulevard (also known as
Assessor’s Parcel Number “APN” 8056-018-005). Surrounding the project site are multi-family
residential located to the north and east, Nettie L. Waite Middle School (across Rosecrans Avenue)
to the south and a vacant lot to the west. It has a general plan designation of Neighborhood
Commercial and zoning of Restricted Commercial (C-1).

PDP No. 2022-04 and DAR No. 2022-05 were approved by the Planning Commission for the
demolition of an existing two-story commercial building (2,500 sq. ft.) and the construction of a new
two-story commercial building totaling 8,715 square feet.
The proposed development includes office, retail, and restaurant tenant spaces. DAR No. 2022-05
was approved to allow a six percent reduction in the required number of parking spaces from 34 to
32 The approved building is designed to comply with all minimum development and architectural
design standards. New parking areas are proposed west and south of the building to provide
convenient access for customers and employees. The approved plans comply with all applicable
code requirements, except for a six percent deficiency in the required number of parking spaces.
To encourage alternative modes of transportation, the project includes seven bicycle parking stalls
located near the southwest corner of the new building. Additional site improvements include
enhanced pedestrian access, upgraded landscaping, and a new trash enclosure integrated within
the new building.

The following table provides a chronological history of the actions taken in relation to the subject
property:

  Approval by Planning Commission for PDP No. 2022-04 and DAR June 14, 2023

  building (2,500 sq. ft.) and the construction of a new two-story
  commercial building totaling 8,715 square feet.
  Planning Commission for ZC No. 2022-02.  June 14, 2023

  Parcel Map No. 83935 recorded date  December 12, 2024

  Approval of a one-year administrative extension request.  June 11, 2024

  Approval of a second one-year administrative extension request.  June 5, 2025
 Norwalk Planning Commission  June 10, 2026

Analysis:

The applicant submitted a request to obtain a third and final one-year extension on May 4, 2026
(see Attachment “B”). Their letter indicates that ownership is committed to the project and the delay
was attributed to their purchase of the adjacent property.
Staff is aware that the applicant subsequently acquired the property at 12209 Rosecrans Avenue
(8056-018-003), but as of this date, the applicant has not indicated how the additional land square
footage would be incorporated into the design of the proposed project.
As such, it is staff’s assessment that six months should be sufficient extension for the proposed
project to move forward. If approved by the Planning Commission, PDP No. 2022-04 and DAR No.
2022-05 would extend the entitlements for another six months with a new expiration of December
14, 2026. Therefore, plans must be submitted for plan check review, permits obtained, and the
project must have undergone a first inspection to maintain the entitlements active by the new
expiration date. Should the project not comply with those parameters, the entitlements will expire.
This is final allowable time extension request.
Environmental Assessment:

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project will not have a significant
effect on the environment and is listed as Class 3 and Class 32 Categorical Exemptions. Class 3
Exemption consists of the construction of new small structures and Class 32 Exemption involves in-
fill development within urbanized areas. The proposed project involves the construction of an 8,715
sq. ft. commercial building and associated site improvements. A Notice of Exemption was posted
on August 21, 2023.
Recommendation:

Should the Planning Commission approve the applicant’s third and final request to extend the
entitlements for an additional six months, the entitlements to commence construction will remain
valid until December 14, 2026.

Request:

That the Chair appoint a member of the Planning Commission to serve on the Art in Public Places
Advisory Committee.
Introduction/background:

Chapter 15.44 of the Norwalk Municipal Code creates the City’s Art in Public Places Program
(APPC) and Section 15.44.060 provides, in part, that the Committee membership shall include a
member of the Planning Commission appointed by the Planning Commission Chair. The current
appointee, Linda Lopez, has indicated that she can no longer participate in these meetings, so there
is a need to appoint another member to the APPC. The APPC typically meets on the fourth Tuesday
of the month at 5:30 p.m.
Recommendation:
That the Chair appoint a member of the Planning Commission to serve on the Art in Public Places
Advisory Committee.
